claims.text: The federal literature on nitinol, one report of it written by Battelle itself, does not support a Battelle 1948-49 lineage for the alloy. NASA SP-5110, prepared for NASA by Battelle Memorial Institute in 1972, opens: 'Some 10 years ago, Buehler and Wiley of the U.S. Naval Ordnance Laboratory developed a series of engineering alloys that possess a unique mechanical (shape) memory. The generic name of the series of alloys is 55-Nitinol, where Nitinol stands for Nickel Titanium Naval Ordnance Laboratory.' The earliest Naval Ordnance Laboratory nitinol report cited anywhere in its reference list is NOLTR 61-75 of 3 August 1961; US Patent 3,174,851 was filed on 1 December 1961; and NASA CR-1433 of September 1969 records Battelle's own role as a subcontractor to Goodyear Aerospace which 'processed the basic Nitinol rod'. The allegation that Wright-Patterson-sponsored Battelle reports on nickel-titanium alloy from 1948-49 are missing from Air Force and Battelle archives is kept on this board as the allegation it is, and is unsupported by the federal literature opened here.

label: 'UAP Gerb' (Sam)
narrative: UAP Gerb is a pseudonymous open-source investigator who has produced the most granular publicly available reconstruction of how the legacy recovery and reverse-engineering portfolio is organised - not as anecdote, but as org charts, office symbols, statutory authorities and named incumbents. His method is unusual in this field and is why he belongs on this board at tier A: each investigation is a multi-hour documentary built on cited primary documents, and he publishes those citations in the video description. His Battelle investigation (18 February 2024) links directly to the CUFON Project Stork progress reports, the CIA reading room copy of Special Report No. 14, a Black Vault release of the Second Progress Report on Titanium Alloys, AEC research reports at the University of North Texas digital library, and the Defense.gov transcript of the Moultrie roundtable. He runs a corporate-by-corporate series - Battelle, Northrop Grumman, TRW, Lockheed Martin, SAIC, Sandia - and an institution-by-institution series covering the Air Force, Navy, Army, NRO and now MITRE. On 7 August 2026 he published 'The MITRE Corporation - UFO Reverse Engineering, USO Tracking, & Legacy Programs', the named priority for this board, which argues that FFRDCs are the 'missing link' in the whole question: the mechanism by which the government can technically vest programs outside the government while retaining strict control of materials and data, and which arbitrates how much defense contractors are told. His two-part 'Manhattan Project 2.0' / 'Special Access Required' series (1 May and 19 June 2026) is the legal-mechanism argument: that the 1947 effort borrowed the Manhattan Project's compartmentalization wholesale, vested custody of recovered disks in AEC national laboratories, placed the control group under the National Security Council and its 5412 Committee, shielded it statutorily under the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, and that after a 1994 restructuring of the SAP enterprise the portfolio now hides inside 'Non-Covert Action Programs' with managed need-to-know access and waived reporting and budgetary requirements. He solicits first-hand witnesses at UAPGERB@protonmail.com. Ross Coulthart has platformed him repeatedly on NewsNation's Reality Check and said on air that he thinks Gerb is 'on the money'.
